query: Consider the following context: During the hot dip aluminum plating process, components such as sinking rollers, pulling rollers, and guide plates will come into long-term contact with high-temperature liquid aluminum and be corroded by the aluminum liquid, greatly reducing their service life. In that context, which material can be used for prepare parts for the dipping and plating equipment and protect the equipment from erosion, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Using a nickel-based alloy, specifically Inconel 625, for the preparation of parts in the dipping and plating equipment can protect the equipment from erosion by liquid aluminum due to its enhanced resistance to corrosion and high-temperature degradation.
generation.intervention: Application of Inconel 625 as a replacement material for components in contact with high-temperature liquid aluminum
generation.conditions: High-temperature environment of the hot dip aluminum plating process, with temperatures ranging from 600°C to 700°C
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable, adherent oxide layer on the surface of Inconel 625, which acts as a barrier to corrosion
generation.mechanism: The nickel-based alloy resists corrosion by forming a protective oxide layer, which prevents the penetration of liquid aluminum into the material, thereby reducing erosion
generation.predicted_outcome: A reduction in erosion rate of at least 80% compared to currently used materials, resulting in an increase in service life of the equipment components by a factor of 5
generation.baseline: Currently used materials for equipment components, with an average service life of 1000 hours
generation.boundary: Temperature range of 600°C to 700°C, and exposure time to liquid aluminum of up to 1000 hours
generation.uncertainty: The actual performance of Inconel 625 may vary depending on the specific processing conditions and the presence of other corrosive species in the environment

falsification_experiment.design: Immersion test of Inconel 625 specimens in liquid aluminum at 650°C for 1000 hours, with periodic measurements of weight loss and surface morphology
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the weight loss of Inconel 625 exceeds 10% of the initial weight, or if the surface roughness increases by more than 50% after the test, the hypothesis is falsified
